# Story Craft — llms.txt (Agent How-To)

> Extremely short adult fiction (≤5:00 spoken / ~600–750 words) in three genres: **love**, **murder**, **crime-of-passion**.
> Corpus root: `/workspace/story-craft/` (or repo equivalent).

## Read order

1. This file (`llms.txt`)
2. `schema.md` — contracts & fail criteria
3. `data/genres.json` — pick genre id
4. Matching `research/{genre}.md` + `research/cross-cutting.md`
5. `frameworks/beat-sheets/{genre}.json`
6. `frameworks/checklists/universal.md` + genre checklist
7. Optional: `frameworks/examples/*` for cold-open technique (not full-story templates)
8. `research/sources.md` when justifying craft choices

## Mission

Write or evaluate Story Craft scripts that:

- Grab attention in the **beginning** (cold open → stake → care in ~30–60s)
- Escalate in the **middle** (no sag; midpoint turn; character pressure; clear timeline)
- **Punch in the ending** (earned payoff; resonance; genre promise kept)

## Non-negotiable success criteria

A script **FAILS** if any of these are true:

| # | Failure |
|---|---------|
| 1 | Weak / fade-out / soft-landing ending (`ending_strength` < 3) |
| 2 | Missing beginning, middle, or ending as first-class phases |
| 3 | Over 5:00 spoken (~750–900+ words without justification) |
| 4 | Love: no clear HEA or HFN; ambiguous “maybe” |
| 5 | Murder: unsolved shrug OR reveal that invents decisive facts |
| 6 | Crime of passion: irreversible act off-page OR no aftermath cost |
| 7 | CSAM / prohibited content |
| 8 | Substantial copyrighted prose pasted from sources |

**Brilliant hooks do not compensate for weak endings.**

## Writing algorithm

```
SELECT genre from data/genres.json
LOAD beat sheet; note act_phase on every beat
NAME single_effect (Poe) in one sentence
PLAN ending FIRST (crisis → climax → resonant coda + opening echo)
DRAFT beginning cold open (plant token)
DRAFT middle escalation (midpoint flip; narrow exits)
DRAFT ending punch (must hurt to cut last 30–40 words)
TRIM to ≤5:00; multi-function details; ≤4 names; no B-plot
RUN universal checklist + genre checklist
EMIT evaluation object from schema.md
IF ending_strength < 3 OR any hard fail → REVISE ending before delivery
```

## Act phase duties (all genres)

### Beginning (~0:00–1:00)
- Cold open into a specific moment (Handley) — not warm reportage
- Stake + why we care within ~30–60 seconds
- Genre promise signaled
- Plant detail/token for ending echo

### Middle (~1:00–3:30)
- Causal escalation; attempts worsen situation
- Midpoint changes meaning or stakes (Yorke)
- Character pressure; timeline clarity
- Micro status changes often enough to prevent sag
- Murder: plant fair dual-reading clues; Passion: close exits; Love: adhesion + wound-based rupture

### Ending (~3:30–5:00) — REQUIRED HIGH STRENGTH
- Love: costly choice + unmistakable HEA/HFN + echo
- Murder: fair reassembly reveal + consequence + echo
- Passion: on-page irreversible act + aftermath cost + token echo
- Surprising yet inevitable; cut after the punch (no lecture fade)

## Genre engines (do not conflate)

| Genre | Engine | Ending promise |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| love | Intimacy vs wound | HEA or HFN earned |
| murder | Fair clue craft / suspense | Reveal reclassifies plants + cost |
| crime-of-passion | Obsession → rupture | Act + moral/emotional aftermath |

Crime-of-passion is **not** “murder with feelings.” Murder lane can include passion motives but still owes fair play if sold as puzzle.

## Output expectations

When producing a story, return:

1. Title + genre id  
2. Estimated word count + spoken seconds  
3. Beat map (`beat_id` → one-line fulfillment) including **ending beats**  
4. Full script text  
5. Evaluation object (`pass`, `ending_strength`, flags)

When evaluating only: evaluation object + concrete revise notes focused on weakest act phase (usually ending).

## Citations policy

Summarize craft ideas; cite titles/URLs from `research/sources.md`. Never paste long copyrighted excerpts into scripts or notes.

## Out of scope

- No other product repos  
- No additional genres beyond the three  
- Site app lives alongside this corpus; prefer `/llms.txt` + `/data/*` on the deployed site for agents
